Case Study: A Drone's Ascent

Read the passage carefully, then answer the 5 MCQs in the test below.

The physics club launches a small quadcopter drone straight up and studies its motion with calculus. Sensors show its vertical velocity, in metres per second, to be v(t)=10-10t, where t is the time in seconds after launch. Because height is the quantity whose rate of change is velocity, the drone's height h(t) must be an antiderivative of v(t). Integrating gives a whole family of height functions h(t)=10t-5t²+C, one for each value of the constant C. The members of this family are identical parabolas shifted vertically: they share the same velocity at every instant but start from different heights. The club launches identical drones from the ground, from a 15 m rooftop and from a tall mast, then compares the three flights recorded on the same graph.
